tier_reason: First-party k6 suite by the swerver author (harness public in swerver-benchmarks: docker-compose.yml, servers/*/Dockerfile, servers/nginx/config/nginx.conf, k6/scenarios/*.js) with swerver built ReleaseFast and nginx from the OpenResty alpine image at OpenResty's default -O2, but the hardware is only 'Docker Desktop on macOS Apple Silicon' with no chip model, so it falls short of A; no independent nginx comparison found.

corrections.baseline: nginx (openresty/openresty:alpine Docker image, unpinned tag; tuned nginx.conf with worker_processes auto, reuseport, 'return 200' for /health and content_by_lua for /echo)
corrections.compiler_and_flags: swerver (April 2026 results, harness commit f5eb7c1): Zig 0.16.0-dev.3133+5ec8e45f3 aarch64-linux, zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast (servers/swerver/Dockerfile); HEAD now builds a bench app with .ReleaseFast hard-coded in servers/swerver/app/build.zig on Zig 0.16.0. nginx: openresty/openresty:alpine image, whose OpenResty configure adds -O2 by default (util/configure) and whose Dockerfile passes only -D/-I cc-opts, so nginx is built at -O2, not -O3.
corrections.hardware: Docker Desktop VM on macOS Apple Silicon (chip not stated), 2 CPUs and 512 MB per server container via docker-compose limits, k6 load generator in an unconstrained container on the same VM, April 2026
corrections.caveats: First-party benchmark by the swerver author, single run reported (no medians or repeat counts). Hot endpoints (/health, /plaintext, /json) are served from a per-second-refreshed pre-encoded response cache that skips the router, middleware and encoder, and the HEAD bench config sets disable_middleware: true; nginx answers /health with 'return 200' and /echo through content_by_lua. swerver container runs with seccomp unconfined so io_uring is used; nginx uses epoll. nginx is built at -O2 (OpenResty default), not -O3. Worker counts are not pinned equal (nginx worker_processes auto; swerver --workers defaults to 1 per its README, April image ran it without a config). Hardware is an unnamed Apple Silicon chip under Docker Desktop's VM. Results are mixed: mixed workload 36,929 vs nginx 36,969 (tie), /echo latency scenario nginx 8,659 vs swerver 8,517, actix-web ahead of swerver on TLS throughput (171,726 vs 161,781), h2 throughput (129,428 vs 111,698) and error handling (141,755 vs 114,455). The native wrk table (274,617 req/s on /health) has no nginx row. swerver's own README concedes feature-stripped reference servers edge it by 1-2% on raw HTTP/1.1 HttpArena tests. The harness has changed since the April results (Jul 2026 commit 'serve the benchmark endpoints + unbreak the baseline build'), so HEAD does not reproduce the measured build exactly.
corrections.why_faster: Server design rather than the Zig language: io_uring backend (seccomp unconfined) against nginx's epoll, a pre-encoded per-second response cache for hot endpoints that skips router, middleware and encoder, and middleware disabled in the bench config, while nginx runs Lua for /echo (swerver-benchmarks README, docker-compose.yml, servers/swerver/config.json, servers/nginx/config/nginx.conf).

notes: All claimed numbers match the swerver-benchmarks README tables (throughput 147,435 vs 118,061; connections 90,657 vs 19,206, page states 4.7x; rapid-fire 143,437 vs 125,346; error handling 114,455 vs 80,053; TLS h2 /health 161,781 vs 107,741). For wave 14 the win is not a language-level one: different server architectures (io_uring plus response cache vs epoll nginx), nginx at -O2 rather than -O3, so same_algorithm and same_opt_level are false; the baseline is tuned, not crippled, so tier C stands. License MIT, 35 stars, 1 fork, not a fork, last commit 2026-09-24 confirmed on github.com; swerver also appears to be submitted to HttpArena (MDA2AV/HttpArena, which carries h2o but no visible nginx entry), whose leaderboard site was not checked.
